attributes.name: caption
rules: Must be nonblank plain text.

attributes.name: columns
rules: A JSON array of 1..16 nonblank plain-text column labels.

attributes.name: caption-visible
rules: Boolean literal true or false; defaults to false.
Content consists only of table rows and supported template control flow.

attributes.name: id
rules: Use alone, not with id-prefix or key; 1..128 ASCII letters, digits, hyphen, underscore, or colon.

attributes.name: id-prefix
rules: Use together with key and not with id; 1..128 ASCII letters, digits, hyphen, underscore, or colon.

attributes.name: key
rules: Use only with id-prefix; one whole checked field resolving to a string, integer, unsigned integer, or model reference; runtime token is 1..128 ASCII letters, digits, hyphen, or underscore, with no sanitization.
Choose exactly id OR id-prefix plus key.
Each row has exactly the table's column count in paired, attribute-free cells, with whitespace only between cells.
Do not put conditional control flow around cells; conditionals inside a cell are supported.
The app must provide stable, globally unique emitted IDs. Literal duplicates within this table are rejected; runtime-generated duplicates are not all detected.

Content may contain text, escaped bindings, HTML including registered route links, and nested supported cui-* declarations admitted by the host; this is host admission, not a raw HTML string property.
No colspan or invented sorting or pagination behavior.

examples.name: rich-customers
requirements: App provides customers as a list of records: id is a safe token string or checked integer/reference; name and email are strings; active and has_scheme are Bool fields.

Host admits cui-badge and cui-empty-state in cell content; app provides stable unique customer IDs.

{% for customer in customers %} {{ customer.name }}
{{ customer.email }} {% if customer.active %}{% else %}{% endif %} {% if customer.has_scheme %}{% else %}{% endif %} {% else %} —— {% endfor %}

rules: The host verifies row and cell structure, labels, budgets, bindings, and stable IDs before admission; package metadata does not grant host capabilities.
No arbitrary raw HTML string properties are supported.

attributes.name: label
rules: Must be nonblank plain text.

attributes.name: variant
rules: One of standard, outlined, or compact; defaults to standard.
Content consists only of self-closing page helpers and supported template control flow.

attributes.name: kind
rules: One of previous, page, current, next, or gap.

attributes.name: label
rules: A literal or one whole checked string field; must be nonblank plain text.

attributes.name: href
rules: Use a safe internal literal or one whole named route call when this item is enabled and navigable.

attributes.name: disabled
rules: Boolean literal true or false; current items cannot be disabled. Disabled navigable items must not have href; use disabled previous/next items for unavailable adjacent pages.

attributes.name: current
rules: Only valid for kind=current; literal true or false, or one whole checked boolean field. Current items cannot have href or be disabled.
Current and gap items cannot have href; gaps are noninteractive.
Enabled previous, page, and next items require href; disabled navigable items must not have href.
kind=current emits aria-current only when current is omitted, true, or a bound Bool evaluates true; false renders an unmarked span. The final navigation must contain exactly one marked current item.

examples.name: customer-pages
requirements: Register customers_page route accepting page if using the navigation links.
App provides has_previous and has_next as Bool fields, previous_page and next_page with the route's declared page argument type, and page_number as a formatted string label.
The app/host must ensure the rendered navigation has exactly one current page item and valid page ranges.
examples.summary: Previous and next destinations are conditional while a current page is marked explicitly.
examples.template:
<cui-pagination label="Customer pages">
  {% if has_previous %}<cui-page kind="previous" label="Previous" href="{{ routes.customers_page(page=previous_page) }}" />{% else %}<cui-page kind="previous" label="Previous" disabled="true" />{% endif %}
  <cui-page kind="current" label="{{ page_number }}" current="true" />
  {% if has_next %}<cui-page kind="next" label="Next" href="{{ routes.customers_page(page=next_page) }}" />{% endif %}
</cui-pagination>

rules: At least one current helper declaration is required lexically by expansion; ensure the final host-rendered output has exactly one current item.
Host route registration, route argument/type checks, destination safety, binding types, and runtime page/range admission remain host-owned; package metadata does not establish these guarantees.
Labels and destinations are emitted as escaped text and attributes.

attributes.name: placeholder
rules: Plain text literal or whole checked string field.

attributes.name: hint
rules: Plain text literal or whole checked string field.

attributes.name: error
rules: Plain text literal or whole checked string field.

attributes.name: required
rules: Boolean literal true or false.

attributes.name: disabled
rules: Boolean literal true or false.

attributes.name: choices
rules: Alternative to child options: JSON array of typed choice objects; cannot be combined with child options.
Canonical paired template form uses cui-option children. The existing JSON choices property is the alternative static-data form; do not combine the two.
The component can also be used self-closing with choices JSON where the host declaration syntax permits it.
Options are plain text only; no rich option markup.

attributes.name: value
rules: A literal or one whole checked string field.

attributes.name: label
rules: A literal or one whole checked string field.

attributes.name: disabled
rules: Boolean literal true or false.
Option values must be unique and nonblank; selected must match an enabled option.
The helper has no body or markup content.

examples.name: customer-status
requirements: App provides customer.status and status_choices iterable with string value and label fields.
The selected value must match an enabled option; the app owns its form and submission behavior.
examples.summary: A select whose options come from app-owned choices and whose selected value is bound to the customer.
examples.template:
<cui-select-field id="customer-status" name="status" label="Status" selected="{{ customer.status }}">
  {% for choice in status_choices %}
  <cui-option value="{{ choice.value }}" label="{{ choice.label }}" />
  {% endfor %}
</cui-select-field>

rules: Exactly one source of options is used: child options or the choices JSON property.
Whole-field bindings are checked by Native template admission; values and labels are emitted as escaped text.
The app owns form submission, routes, commands, and domain validation.
